ai-factory.notes: Source-reviewed against the AI Factory 2.x snapshot declaring 2.19.0 at commit 3c1ddd4740d7b1c30d8ecb3dc80fa5e7b8d7ef5a (2.18.1...3c1ddd4740d7, 7 commits and 16 changed files). No 2.19.0 Git tag, GitHub release, or npm package existed at review time, so the last exact published-executable consumer smoke remains 2.18.1 and this metadata does not claim a 2.19 release artifact. The 2.19 delta adds upstream-owned /aif-warmup and a root Microsoft APM manifest; AIFHub creates warmup.paths: [] only for fresh configs, preserves existing user-owned lists without backfill, and adds no duplicate warmup skill/injection or APM distribution path. Extension schema/loader, injection and MCP contracts, Node >=18, bin, and dependencies are unchanged. The cumulative reviewed baseline preserves AI Factory 2.13.x plan-aware /aif-commit Commit Plan grouping and /aif-distillation for reusable Agent Skills, AI Factory 2.14 /aif-archive with paths.archive and archive-aware sequential plan behavior, config-aware project utilities /aif-architecture, /aif-docs, and /aif-qa as upstream-owned context outputs, and AI Factory 2.15 managed agent config preservation plus interactive newly available built-in skill update behavior. Headline 2.16-2.17 changes cover revision-bound research context, branch-scoped /aif-qa-check, regression-first /aif-fix evidence, and verbatim Original Request preservation. Direct follow-ups cover QA execution surfaces, collision-resistant branch identity, revision/worktree/source/case freshness, reusable non-sensitive QA memory, authorization and redaction, custom fix-plan preservation, plan/improve Original Request clarifications, Universal / Other MCP through .mcp.json, and project-evidence-backed Control Flow rules. The reviewed 2.17.0...2.18.0 comparison keeps extension schema/loader, injection and MCP contracts, Node >=18, bin and dependencies unchanged; AIFHub therefore adds no speculative runtime adapter. The reviewed 2.18.0...2.18.1 patch contains 2 commits across 8 files and is prompt/docs-only apart from package/test metadata: runtime APIs, extension schema/loader, injection/MCP contracts, Node, bin and dependencies remain unchanged. Its /aif-explore Research Coherence Gate stays upstream-owned; AIFHub supplies only a non-bypass pass-through after permitted persisted writes, with direct fallback when optional Task delegation is unavailable and coherence before the ultra Bundle Integrity Gate. AI Factory 2.18 ultra planning maps to canonical OpenSpec detail in OpenSpec-native mode and remains an upstream-owned marked bundle in legacy mode; ultra research remains revision-bound supporting context. Completed-phase /aif-loop budgeting and skills.sh documentation are reviewed no-ops. The privacy-gated /aif-transfer skill stays upstream-owned and delegates accepted project evidence to /aif-evolve without an AIFHub copy. Plan, explore, improve, implement, verify, fix, archive, rules, commit, roadmap and namespaced-agent consumers retain only their bounded AIFHub/OpenSpec adapters. Reviewed no-ops keep /aif-architecture structure upstream-owned, avoid duplicate generated-rules compiler logic, and do not copy community-extension documentation bodies.

openspec.notes: Validated sequentially from upstream OpenSpec 1.3.1 through 1.12.0, including reviewed prerelease 1.6.0-beta.1, while keeping the supported stable CLI range >=1.3.1 <2.0.0; prereleases remain unsupported for production capabilities. OpenSpec 1.12.0 adds optional bulk validation findings reports, advisory INFO archive preflight, empty-directory .gitkeep anchors, SourceCraft Code Assistant, and repository-grounded propose/ff guidance. AIFHub preserves full per-change validation reports, INFO diagnostics and fail-closed archive behavior, adds bounded read-only code grounding to plan/improve, and leaves report selection, generated tools, init/update and package lifecycle upstream-owned. OpenSpec 1.11.0 adds optional show --diff and status --all, strict Purpose placeholder diagnostics, archive rename ordering, atomic schema init --default, and Antigravity shared .agents migration. AIFHub preserves per-change orchestration and existing show argv, adds Purpose authoring/remediation guidance, and verifies exact CLI regressions without expanding the public adapter. Batch JSON failures retain per-change diagnostics and exit 1. Schema, Antigravity, Explore confirmation, Fish completions and generated tool workflows remain upstream-owned. OpenSpec 1.10.0 adds Zed and init language tooling, inline task verification guidance, store-aware specs instructions, native skip metadata for schemas without a specs artifact, bounded capability-retirement diagnostics, stderr-only telemetry notices, package lifecycle cleanup, custom-profile dependency repair, and upstream generated-asset/update fixes. AIFHub mirrors only the inline task verification rule in its plan/refinement prompts, advances reviewed-version metadata, preserves open JSON envelopes and fail-closed diagnostics, accepts native skip_specs for no-spec schemas, and leaves Zed, language init, Stores, profiles, update, generated assets, and package management upstream-owned. OpenSpec 1.9.0 adds strict task-numbering diagnostics, nested scenario-loss validation, root-selection behavior, archive serialization fixes, telemetry-free JSON, and upstream command/schema/agent generation changes. AIFHub preserves strict fail-closed diagnostics, treats non-strict task-numbering warnings as observations, retains rootless built-in schemas success and rootless list/bulk validation failure semantics, and leaves Command Code, schema, Store, tool, agent, skill, and package ownership upstream. OpenSpec 1.8.0 adds explicit retire_capabilities metadata, scenario-loss validation, nested task progress, non-TTY archive guidance, and new agent targets. AIFHub version-gates retirement metadata in its planning prompt, preserves fail-closed validation diagnostics, already counts nested task checkboxes, and leaves agent generation upstream-owned. OpenSpec 1.7.0 adds native skip_specs metadata, apply/archive instructions, numeric-leading change IDs, nested spec folders, UTF-8 BOM handling, a default Store, new tool adapters, and a self-upgrading openspec update. AIFHub honors native .openspec.yaml skip_specs during artifact validation and all-change sync, keeps recursive nested-spec discovery, supports archive instructions through the shared runner, and preserves the older numeric-ID status fallback for pre-1.7 CLIs. OpenSpec 1.6.0 unifies validate/view/archive resolution, makes archive validation failures exit non-zero, handles nested specs and task files, adds /opsx:update, Oh My Pi and Trae support, and fixes requirement parsing, archive drift, skill permissions, and fresh Store registration. OpenSpec 1.5.0 introduces Stores in very early beta, fixes config parsing and CRLF YAML frontmatter generation, and adds an additive root field to command JSON. AIFHub remains adapter-only and does not install or manage OpenSpec skills, /opsx:* commands, tool integrations, Stores, workspace beta state, agent targets, or openspec update.
